text: The blood type is A+ and the Coombs test is negative, which rules out blood group incompatibility as the cause of jaundice. speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast Milk Jaundice.

The clinical picture of prolonged unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in a well-appearing, exclusively breastfed 2-week-old, with negative workup for hemolysis, infection, biliary atresia, and other causes, is classic for benign breast milk jaundice. The family history of a sibling with liver issues is concerning for genetic causes, but in the absence of cholestasis or other abnormalities, breast milk jaundice remains the most likely diagnosis; however, I recommend pausing breastfeeding for 24 hours to see if bilirubin levels drop, while continuing to pump to maintain supply.
